title: feat: add `pie` langium parser
body:
## :bookmark_tabs: Summary

- Create `pie` langium parser and integrate it in `packages/mermaid`.
- ignore `yaml`, `comments`, and `directives` in `pie` grammar

### BREAKING CHANGES

- Remove `cleanValue` from `pieDb`.
- Rename `D3Sections` into `D3Section`
- Change `addSection` header into `D3Section` type

### Issues

- Resolves #2472
- Partially #4401

## :straight_ruler: Design Decisions

### :clipboard: Tasks

Make sure you

- [x] :book: have read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] :computer: have added necessary unit/e2e tests.
author: Yokozuna59

comments.body: Why is this required?

comments.author: Yokozuna59
comments.body:
The `.replace(/"/g, '')` part is essential because the rule matches everything between double quotes including the wrapper quotes, so we manually have to remove it.

The other two lines are to clean the what is between doable quotes, the current render does that:

```
pie showData
    "dog": 1
    "            cat      ":1
    "                          ": 1  
```

```mermaid
pie showData
    "dog": 1
    "            cat      ":1
    "                          ": 1  
```

comments.author: Yokozuna59
comments.body: I think we should also remove newlines since they're also removed in layout.

comments.body: `.replaceAll(/[\t ]{2,}/gm, ' ')` I don't think we should be doing this. Trimming the ends is fine, but we should not be changing things inside the user input.

comments.body:
I wouldn't recommend name the abstract class as `MermaidTokenBuilder`, it would confuse contributors when implementing new parser.
We mostly extend `Common...` classes in other diagram services, but when it comes to `TokenBuilder`, extending`MermaidTokenBuilder` is kinda weird.

comments.author: sidharthv96
comments.body:
`MermaidTokenBuilder` -> The abstract class 
`CommonTokenBuilder` -> Implementation of MermaidTokenBuilder that is used only in places where a specific TokenBuilder is not necessary
`<Diagram>TokenBuilder` -> Implementation of MermaidTokenBuilder for that particular diagram.

comments.author: Yokozuna59
comments.body:
As I said, it won't be possible unless we allowed undesired grammar.

> I don't think so, unless we broke or allowed something that shouldn't be allowed.
> I don't think it's even possible in jison.
>
> https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/pull/4799#discussion_r1313964781

In your code, you used `\s+` as a hidden rule, which means ignore all whitespaces characters, so the following code would be allowed:

```
pie 



showData "section1":
1 "section2":
2
```

comments.author: Yokozuna59
comments.body:
Another possible approach is to use `EOL`, but `EOF` isn't currently supported: https://github.com/eclipse-langium/langium/pull/1162

```langium
fragment EOL:
  NEWLINE+ | EOF
;
```

> https://github.com/eclipse-langium/langium/pull/1162#issuecomment-1687714247

comments.author: Yokozuna59
comments.body:
I think we could use this approach; the `grammar` parameter would have the array of rules as it has been declared in the `.langium`, declared rules at the beginning and imported rules at the end. Then we could have a pivot rule (in this case it's `TitleAndAccessibilities`), and flip all other rules around it. After that, `super.buildTokens` should just sort them in terms of efficiency.

For example: `[1,2,3,4,5]` with pivot 3 should return `[4,5,3,1,2]`.

CC @weedySeaDragon
